attributes.title: Level 4

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓ What function can be used to convert number variables to string values so that they can be pushed to the words array?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What type of values can be stored in the words array?


Solution: 

The toString function .toString() should be added inside the parentheses of the push code on lines 11 and 13.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Notice the error message on the bottom says the problem is on Lines 11 and 13: the argument of type ‘number’ is not assignable to parameter of type ‘string’.



Fix the bugs in the code so that the 2 number variables can be pushed to the words array.

subgroups.title: Debugging Nested Arrays
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

validationItems.text: .toString() added inside the parentheses of the push code on lines 11 and 13.
validationItems.failureText: Try adding a function to convert the 2 number variables to string values.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ What symbols are used to declare a list of elements in a nested array?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What symbols contain all of the elements in an array?


Solution: 

Opening and closing brackets should be added on Lines 15 and 18 to surround both arrays of elements in the userName array.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the correct symbols surround the arrays of elements nested inside the userName array.

subgroups.title: Debugging Nested Arrays
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

validationItems.text: Opening and closing brackets added to surround both arrays of elements in the userName array.
validationItems.failureText: Try updating the index values used in each array of elements in the userName array.

requirements.match:
let userName = [
    [words[2], words[0], words[3]],
    [words[2], words[0], words[3]]
]

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ Which index values might be used in the second array of elements of the userName array so that a different combination of usernames will appear?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What variables might be combined to form a different username suggestion?


Solution: 

Index values in the second array of elements in the userName array should be changed, so that they are different from the first.
steps.instructions:
When the dialog boxes appear, the same username suggestion is shared!


Fix the bugs in the code so that a different combination of index values from the words array are shared in each dialog box.

subgroups.name: solve 4

steps.hints: ❓ What symbols should be added to the string separation parameter inside the parentheses of the join function so that the values appear without any spaces or symbols between them?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which symbols tell the program what to place between each value combined by the join function?


Solution: 

Quotation marks “” should be added inside the parentheses of the join function on line 23.
steps.instructions:
When the dialog boxes appear, each value in the username suggestion is separated by a comma.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the values in the username appear without any spaces or symbols between them.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of Purple Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about arrays and array functions. You’ll build on your understanding of arrays in JavaScript by exploring functions that will help you access, modify, and join elements in an array. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 4:

badges.title: Push It, Pop It, Join It, Concat It!
badges.description: Use several different array functions in JavaScript to access and modify the data stored inside an array.

badges.title: A String of Numbers
badges.description: Use the toString function to convert a number to a string

badges.title: Arrays All The Way Down
badges.description: Create a nested array in JavaScript.

badges.title: Joined at the Hip
badges.description: Use the join function to join all the elements of a string array into one string value.

badges.title: Together Forever
badges.description: Use the concat function to join two arrays together into one new array.

badges.title: Pop It Like It’s Hot
badges.description: Use the pop function to remove and return the last element from an array.

badges.title: Group Project
badges.description: Use the allOfKind function to create an array of all sprites of the specified sprite kind.
